beats.text: Three doors. Behind one, a car. Behind the other two, goats.
The host knows where the car is. He opens door three. A goat.
Then he asks: do you want to switch to door two?
Most people say it doesn't matter. Two doors left. Fifty-fifty.
Your first pick had a one in three chance. Opening a door doesn't change that.
The other two thirds didn't vanish. The host packed them into the one door he left closed.
Staying wins about a third of the time. Switching wins two thirds.
